title: Learning Reachability-Based Safety Representations for Real-Time Robot Navigation in Unknown and Dynamic Environments
abstract: arXiv:2610.16522v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Safe robot navigation in unknown, dynamic environments requires more than geometric collision checking: a robot still far from an obstacle may be unable to avoid it because of its speed, orientation, or the obstacle's motion. Hamilton--Jacobi (HJ) reachability analysis captures this in a value function whose sign separates states that admit a safe continuation from those where collision is unavoidable, but computing it online for every newly observed environment is too expensive. This dissertation trains neural implicit representations offline on reachability solutions to give optimization-based controllers this information in real time. Since the value function never exceeds the constraint, it equals a directly computed constraint, such as a signed distance, minus a nonnegative dynamics correction. translated_title: 面向未知动态环境中实时机器人导航的基于可达性的安全表示学习
translated_abstract: 在未知、动态环境中实现安全的机器人导航，仅靠几何碰撞检测是不够的：机器人即使距离障碍物还很远，也可能由于其自身的速度、朝向或障碍物的运动而无法避开它。哈密顿-雅可比（HJ）可达性分析通过一个值函数刻画了这一点，该值函数的符号能够区分可以安全继续运行的状态与碰撞不可避免的状态，但针对每个新观测到的环境在线计算该值函数的代价过于高昂。本论文通过在可达性解上离线训练神经隐式表示，来实时地为基于优化的控制器提供这一信息。由于值函数从不超过约束，它等于一个可直接计算的约束（例如符号距离）减去一个非负的动力学修正项。仅学习这一修正项，即使存在近似误差，也能保证所表示的障碍物始终位于预测安全集之外。
tldr: 本论文通过离线在哈密顿-雅可比可达性解上训练神经隐式表示，并仅学习非负的动力学修正项，使基于优化的控制器能够在未知动态环境中实时获得安全信息，实现实时安全的机器人导航。
en_tdlr: This dissertation trains neural implicit representations offline on Hamilton-Jacobi reachability solutions—learning only a nonnegative dynamics correction—to provide optimization-based controllers with real-time safety information for robot navigation in unknown and dynamic environments.
